passages.p1:
Hi Mia,

Thanks for inviting me to your [[1]] party on Saturday. I'd love to come, but I need to [[2]] my cousin at the airport. Her flight was delayed, so I'm not sure when we'll get back. Could you [[3]] me the address by text? If I arrive late, please don't [[4]] for me before eating. I can [[5]] a sandwich on the way. I hope the weather stays [[6]], since the garden gets muddy after rain.

Best, Sam
passages.p2: Put the sentences in the correct order to make a story. The first one is done for you.
passages.p3:
A. Until well into the nineteenth century, mathematical exclusion was engineered less through explicit claims of female incapacity than through control of the conditions under which expertise could be acquired. Universities, learned societies, observatories, and civil-service examinations either barred women or admitted them without credentials, stipends, or access to advanced lectures. Domestic labour and legal dependence further fragmented uninterrupted study. Consequently, many capable women worked through private tutors, family correspondence, translation, or anonymous problem solving. These improvised channels could generate remarkable competence, yet they rarely conferred the institutional recognition needed to secure posts, pupils, archives, or priority for discoveries.

B. Grace Chisholm Young negotiated this landscape by moving across national systems rather than by receiving uncomplicated admission to one. After studying at Cambridge, where women could sit examinations but were denied degrees, she continued at Göttingen and became one of the first women to earn a doctorate there. Her work ranged across geometry, calculus, and the foundations of analysis; collaborative publications with William Henry Young, however, have often encouraged later readers to dilute her independent intellectual profile. The episode illustrates how a woman’s research could be internationally consequential while the customary markers of scholarly ownership remained unstable.

C. Olga Taussky-Todd’s trajectory shows that mathematical innovation may be dispersed across disciplines and countries. Expelled from the professional prospects of interwar Austria by antisemitic exclusion, she built a career in Britain and the United States. Her investigations of matrices, algebraic number theory, and the spectral properties of operators connected abstract algebra to practical questions in vibration and aeronautics. At the California Institute of Technology, she also cultivated a style of supervision in which difficult linear-algebraic problems were made accessible without being simplified. Her legacy therefore resists the misleading division between pure theory, technical application, and intellectual mentorship.

D. Euphemia Lofton Haynes made mathematics education itself an object of rigorous inquiry rather than a merely administrative concern. In her 1943 doctoral dissertation, she examined the consequences of ability grouping in Washington, DC, public schools, exposing how apparently neutral classification could reproduce racial and social inequality. As a teacher, principal, and school-board member, she combined quantitative reasoning with institutional advocacy. Her intervention matters because it relocates mathematical authority: expertise can reside not only in proving theorems but also in scrutinising the systems that decide who receives advanced instruction. That broader conception remains essential when discussions of participation ignore school-level sorting.

E. Formal prohibitions have often been replaced by mechanisms that appear impartial while distributing opportunity unevenly. Hiring committees may define excellence through uninterrupted publication, prestige networks, and recommendation styles historically easier for men to accumulate. Seminar cultures can assign women disproportionate service, teaching, and representational labour, reducing the protected time required for research. Evaluation then converts these unequal inputs into apparently objective outcomes: fewer invitations, slower promotion, and diminished visibility. The central problem is thus not simply overt hostility. It is the recursive character of organisational judgement, whereby earlier exclusion is repeatedly reclassified as evidence of lesser merit.

F. Recent interventions have altered portions of this ecology. Funded doctoral places, anti-harassment procedures, parental-leave policies, transparent salary audits, and networks such as women-in-mathematics seminars have widened entry and reduced some forms of isolation. Their most durable effect, however, emerges when visible mathematicians do more than furnish inspirational biographies. When senior women and allied colleagues nominate junior researchers for talks, explain tacit conventions, share collaborations, and contest biased assessments, they convert recognition into access. Role models matter not as decorative exceptions but as participants who make an inherited profession navigable for those previously treated as outsiders.

G. Nevertheless, headline gains in undergraduate enrolment should not be mistaken for parity throughout the discipline. Women remain less represented in some mathematically intensive specialisms, in permanent research appointments, and especially in senior professorships and major-prize ecosystems. Aggregated figures can obscure intersecting inequalities associated with race, nationality, disability, and caregiving responsibilities. Moreover, departures are not always individual choices made in a vacuum; they may register accumulated exposure to precarious contracts, credibility challenges, and narrow definitions of success. A serious account of the contemporary gap must therefore track transitions, not merely count entrants.

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

If you _____ to need help, just ask the teacher.
questions.explanation:
If' mang nghĩa 'mỗi khi/nếu' nên dùng hiện tại đơn 'happen', không dùng 'would' trong mệnh đề if.
[TD]Dịch: Nếu bạn tình cờ cần giúp đỡ, cứ hỏi cô giáo.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

He _____ be rich, but he is not very kind to people.
questions.explanation:
May' diễn tả sự nhượng bộ ('có thể đúng là... nhưng...').
[TD]Dịch: Anh ta có thể giàu, nhưng anh ta không tử tế với mọi người lắm.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

If only he _____ smoking when the doctor told him, he would be healthy now.
questions.explanation:
If only' + quá khứ hoàn thành 'had given up' diễn tả tiếc nuối về quá khứ, kéo theo kết quả hiện tại.
[TD]Dịch: Giá mà anh ấy đã bỏ thuốc khi bác sĩ khuyên, thì bây giờ anh ấy đã khỏe mạnh.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

She _____ her assistant of leaking the confidential merger details to a rival firm.
questions.explanation:
Cấu trúc 'accuse sb of + V-ing' (buộc tội ai làm gì) đúng giới từ, khác 'blame sb for'.
[TD]Dịch: Cô ấy buộc tội trợ lý của mình đã làm rò rỉ chi tiết thương vụ sáp nhập mật cho một công ty đối thủ.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

It is reported that the old house _____ to a new owner.
questions.explanation:
Bị động hoàn thành 'has been sold' diễn tả việc ngôi nhà đã được bán.
[TD]Dịch: Có tin rằng ngôi nhà cũ đã được bán cho chủ mới.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

That _____ Tom at the door. He said he would come tonight.
questions.explanation:
Will be' diễn tả sự suy đoán chắc chắn về hiện tại (hẳn là).
[TD]Dịch: Đó hẳn là Tom ở ngoài cửa. Anh ấy nói sẽ đến tối nay.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

He made the decision without asking anyone, and his team _____ it ever since.
questions.explanation:
Hiện tại hoàn thành 'have regretted' với 'ever since' diễn tả sự tiếc nuối kéo dài từ quá khứ đến nay.
[TD]Dịch: Anh ấy đã quyết định mà không hỏi ai, và đội của anh hối tiếc kể từ đó đến giờ.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

In the past, people _____ to bow when they met someone important.
questions.explanation:
Used to' diễn tả phong tục/thói quen từng tồn tại trong quá khứ nay đã mất.
[TD]Dịch: Ngày xưa, mọi người thường cúi chào khi gặp người quan trọng.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

He arrived _____ for the meeting because his flight had been delayed for hours.
questions.explanation:
Cần tính từ/trạng từ 'late' (muộn); 'lately' nghĩa 'gần đây' nên không hợp ngữ cảnh.
[TD]Dịch: Anh ấy đến muộn cuộc họp vì chuyến bay đã bị hoãn nhiều giờ.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

_____ majority of the students passed the test.
questions.explanation:
The majority of' dùng mạo từ xác định 'the' khi nói về đa số một nhóm cụ thể.
[TD]Dịch: Đa số học sinh đã đỗ bài kiểm tra.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

You _____ told me you don't eat meat before I cooked dinner!
questions.explanation:
Might have + V3' diễn tả lời trách móc về việc lẽ ra nên làm.
[TD]Dịch: Lẽ ra bạn nên nói cho tôi biết bạn không ăn thịt trước khi tôi nấu bữa tối chứ![/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

We would have been late _____ the taxi driver's fast driving.
questions.explanation:
But for' nghĩa là 'nếu không có', dẫn danh từ để chỉ nguyên nhân giả định.
[TD]Dịch: Chúng tôi đã bị muộn nếu không nhờ tài xế taxi lái nhanh.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

If you _____ me, I think this movie is not very good.
questions.explanation:
Câu điều kiện thực diễn tả ý kiến hiện tại, dùng hiện tại đơn 'ask' trong mệnh đề if.
[TD]Dịch: Nếu bạn hỏi tôi, tôi nghĩ bộ phim này không hay lắm.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

You can borrow my flat in Vienna _____ you water the plants and feed the cat.
questions.explanation:
As long as' nêu điều kiện (miễn là), phù hợp ngữ cảnh cho phép có kèm điều kiện.
[TD]Dịch: Bạn có thể mượn căn hộ của tôi ở Vienna miễn là bạn tưới cây và cho mèo ăn.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

_____ you happen to see Lan at school, please give her this book.
questions.explanation:
If + happen to' diễn tả tình huống tình cờ; dùng 'If' cho điều kiện thông thường.
[TD]Dịch: Nếu bạn tình cờ gặp Lan ở trường, hãy đưa cho cô ấy cuốn sách này.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

_____ the bridge been built stronger, it wouldn't be damaged now.
questions.explanation:
Đảo ngữ câu điều kiện: 'Had + chủ ngữ + V3' thay cho 'If... had' diễn tả giả định trái với quá khứ.
[TD]Dịch: Giá như cây cầu được xây chắc hơn, thì bây giờ nó đã không bị hỏng.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

Direct: 'You shouldn't have spent so much money on that toy.' Reported: Mom told me I _____ so much money on that toy.
questions.explanation:
Shouldn't have + V3' đã ở quá khứ nên giữ nguyên khi tường thuật.
[TD]Dịch: Mẹ nói lẽ ra tôi không nên tiêu nhiều tiền vào món đồ chơi đó.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

I found a girl _____ voice is really beautiful.
questions.explanation:
Whose' là đại từ quan hệ chỉ sở hữu, thay cho 'the girl's voice'.
[TD]Dịch: Tôi tìm thấy một cô gái mà giọng hát rất hay.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

I will lend you my bike _____ that you return it by Friday.
questions.explanation:
On condition (that)' nêu điều kiện ràng buộc (với điều kiện là).
[TD]Dịch: Tôi sẽ cho bạn mượn xe đạp với điều kiện bạn trả lại trước thứ Sáu.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

My friend _____ going to the new restaurant for dinner.
questions.explanation:
Động từ 'suggest' đi với V-ing (không dùng 'suggest sb to do').
[TD]Dịch: Bạn tôi đề nghị đi ăn tối ở nhà hàng mới.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

_____ have a quick coffee somewhere before catching the late train?
questions.explanation:
Shall we...?' dùng để đưa ra lời đề nghị, rủ rê cùng làm gì đó.
[TD]Dịch: Chúng ta đi uống cà phê nhanh đâu đó trước khi bắt chuyến tàu muộn nhé?[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

You look tired!' 'Yes, I _____ for the test since this morning.'
questions.explanation:
Hiện tại hoàn thành tiếp diễn 'have been studying' diễn tả hành động kéo dài từ 'since this morning' đến hiện tại.
[TD]Dịch: 'Trông cậu mệt quá!' 'Ừ, tớ đã ôn thi từ sáng đến giờ.'[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

He was writing his essay when the lights went off, and he realized he _____ to save it.
questions.explanation:
Quá khứ hoàn thành 'had forgotten' diễn tả việc quên xảy ra trước thời điểm mất điện.
[TD]Dịch: Anh ấy đang viết bài luận thì đèn tắt, và anh nhận ra mình đã quên lưu bài.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

The plan has been _____ for several weeks.
questions.explanation:
Cụm danh từ 'under consideration' (đang được xem xét) tránh thể bị động.
[TD]Dịch: Kế hoạch đã được xem xét trong vài tuần.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

The proposal was _____ rejected by the entire board without further discussion.
questions.explanation:
Trạng từ 'flatly' (thẳng thừng) đi với 'rejected'; 'very/rather' không bổ nghĩa cho động từ kiểu này.
[TD]Dịch: Đề xuất bị cả hội đồng thẳng thừng bác bỏ mà không bàn bạc thêm.[/TD]

The first meal you eat in the morning
questions.explanation:
breakfast (noun) the first meal you eat in the morning (bữa ăn đầu tiên trong ngày mà bạn ăn vào buổi sáng sớm)
I have eggs for breakfast. (Tôi ăn trứng vào bữa sáng.)

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Vocabulary

A place where people buy and sell food and other things
questions.explanation:
market (noun) a place where people buy and sell food and other things (nơi mọi người tập trung để mua bán thực phẩm và các hàng hóa khác)
My mother goes to the market every morning. (Mẹ tôi đi chợ mỗi buổi sáng.)

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Vocabulary

The study of the world and how things work
questions.explanation:
science (noun) the study of the world and how things work (môn học nghiên cứu về thế giới tự nhiên và cách mọi thứ vận hành)
Science is my favourite subject. (Khoa học là môn học yêu thích của tôi.)

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Vocabulary

Saying no, or being bad and unhappy
questions.explanation:
negative (adjective) saying no, or being bad and unhappy (thể hiện sự phủ nhận, từ chối hoặc cảm xúc tiêu cực và không tốt)
Try not to have a negative feeling. (Hãy cố gắng không có cảm xúc tiêu cực.)

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Vocabulary

Showing who is meant to get or use something
questions.explanation:
for (preposition) showing who is meant to get or use something (dùng để chỉ ra đối tượng hoặc mục đích mà điều gì đó được dành riêng)
This gift is for you. (Món quà này là dành cho bạn.)

questions.explanation: marking = chấm

questions.explanation: development = phát triển

questions.content:

questions.explanation: qualifications = bằng cấp

questions.content:

questions.explanation: extensive = trên diện rộng

Being a good doctor ___ a lot of skill, patience and years of training.
questions.explanation: demands = đòi hỏi

Your friend has posted: “I’m moving to a new apartment next week. I’m so excited!” Write a reply. Congratulate your friend and tell them about your own home. Write 20–30 words.
questions.sampleAnswer: Congratulations on your new apartment! My flat is small but cosy, and I love cooking in my bright kitchen every evening.

questions.content:
Writing — Part 3 - Three responses

My advice is to save as much money as possible before buying. You should also research property prices, mortgage rates, and planned developments in different areas. This can help you avoid making an expensive mistake.

Writing — Part 3 - Three responses

I think young people should rent a home before they decide to buy one. Renting lets you try living in a neighbourhood and understand your monthly costs without making such a long-term financial commitment.

Writing — Part 3 - Three responses

For me, location is more important than the size or appearance of a property. A home near public transport, shops, schools, and workplaces can save time every day and may increase in value later.

Writing — Part 4 - Informal and formal emails

Write an informal email to your friend, Mai. Tell her about your experience of house-hunting, explain what you learned, and offer to help her. Write about 40-50 words.
questions.sampleAnswer:
Hi Mai,

I spent six months looking for my first flat, and I learned to check the area at different times, compare total costs, and never rush after one viewing. I can help you make a checklist or visit properties with you this weekend.

Best,
Linh

questions.content:
Writing — Part 4 - Informal and formal emails

Write a formal email to the editor of a community website. Propose writing an article with tips for young home buyers. Explain your qualifications and outline how you would structure the article. Write about 120-150 words.
questions.sampleAnswer:
Dear Editor,

I would like to propose an article for your community website entitled "Buying Your First Home: Practical Advice for Young Adults." As a housing adviser at a local credit union and a recent first-time buyer, I have helped young people understand budgets, mortgages, and property searches. I also completed a short course in personal finance last year.

The article would begin with a simple checklist for calculating an affordable budget, including deposit, legal fees, insurance, and monthly repayments. Next, it would explain how readers can research neighbourhoods, compare mortgage offers, and inspect a property carefully. Finally, I would include common mistakes to avoid, such as borrowing too much or ignoring repair costs, plus links to free local support services.

This clear, step-by-step format would make reliable advice accessible to inexperienced buyers. I would be pleased to submit a draft next week.

Yours faithfully,
Linh Tran

Sắp xếp các câu theo thứ tự đúng:

  1. Every film begins with a simple idea that a writer develops into a script.
  2. During filming, however, scenes are often shot out of sequence to save time and money.
  3. Finally, music, sound effects and visual effects are added before the finished film is shown to audiences.
  4. Once the script is complete, producers use it to make a budget and select a director.
  5. When the shooting is over, editors assemble the best footage and create the final version of the story.
  6. After the director has chosen the cast, crew and locations, the cameras can start recording.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 1 - Personal information

Can you describe your room? What does it look like, what furniture do you have, and what is your favourite thing in your room?
questions.sampleAnswer: My room is small but bright. The walls are white, and there is a big window near my bed. I have a bed, a desk, a chair, and a wardrobe. My favourite thing is my desk because I study and draw there.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 1 - Personal information

What activities do you do with your family? When do you do them, and how often?
questions.sampleAnswer: I often cook dinner with my family at weekends. My mother makes soup, and I wash vegetables or set the table. We also watch a film together on Sunday evening. We do these activities once or twice a week because everyone is usually busy.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 1 - Personal information

What do you usually do with friends in your free time? Where do you go, and why do you enjoy it?
questions.sampleAnswer: In my free time, I usually meet my friends at a café near our school. We talk, drink juice, and sometimes play board games. I like being with them because we laugh a lot and I can forget about homework for a while.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 2 - Describe a picture

Describe the picture.
questions.sampleAnswer: In this picture, I can see four friends sitting around a table. They are playing a board game together in a bright room. There is a large game board in the middle of the table, and I can see small pieces and some cards on it. One young woman is holding a card in her hand. A man next to her is moving a game piece. The other two friends are watching the game carefully. All of them are smiling or laughing, so they look very happy. I think someone has just done something funny or won a point. There are also drinks and snacks on the table. The room looks comfortable and friendly. In my opinion, they are having a great time because they can talk, laugh, and enjoy the game together.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 2 - Describe a picture

Do you prefer board games or video games? Why?
questions.sampleAnswer: I think board games are better than video games when I am with friends. We can sit together, talk, and see each other’s faces. Board games also make us laugh when somebody makes a mistake. Video games can be exciting, but people sometimes look only at the screen. For me, board games are more friendly and social, especially at weekends.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 2 - Describe a picture

How important is it to spend time with friends?
questions.sampleAnswer: I think spending time with friends is very important. Friends can make us feel happy when we are tired or sad. We can talk about school, work, and our problems. They can also give us useful advice. I like meeting my friends for coffee, a meal, or a game. These simple activities help us feel less lonely and make our friendship stronger.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 3 - Compare two pictures

Compare these two pictures.
questions.sampleAnswer: In both pictures, I can see young people travelling in a city. In the first picture, a young woman is sitting on a bus. She is wearing casual clothes and looking out of the window. The bus looks quite busy, and she is not driving. She can relax, read, or use her phone during the journey. In the second picture, a young man is riding a bicycle on a city street. He is wearing a helmet and moving between cars and buildings. He needs to watch the road carefully. The main difference is the type of transport. The woman uses public transport, while the man rides his own bike. The bus may be more comfortable in bad weather, but cycling can be quicker on busy streets at rush hour.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 3 - Compare two pictures

Which do you prefer, travelling by bus or by bicycle? Why?
questions.sampleAnswer: I would prefer to travel by bicycle in my city, especially for short trips. It gives me freedom because I can leave when I want and stop easily. I also enjoy being outside and getting some exercise. However, I would take the bus when it rains, when I carry heavy bags, or when I need to travel a long distance.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 3 - Compare two pictures

What are the advantages of cycling in modern cities?
questions.sampleAnswer: Cycling is good for cities. First, it can reduce traffic because fewer people use cars. It is better for the air because bicycles do not make smoke. Cycling is also good exercise, so people can stay healthy on the way to work or school. It can save money too, because people do not buy fuel or pay bus fares. Cities should build bike lanes for cyclists.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 4 - Discuss an abstract topic

Technology has made many things easier for people. Do you agree? Describe a time when you used technology to help you. How did you feel about using it?
questions.sampleAnswer:
I agree that technology has made many things easier for people. We can talk to family, study, shop, and find information quickly. For example, last month I needed to visit a new hospital in another part of my city. I did not know the way, and I was worried about being late.

I used a map app on my phone. First, I typed the hospital’s name into the app. Then it showed me the best bus to take and told me when to get off. While I was on the bus, I looked at the map again because the streets were new to me. The app also showed a short walk from the bus stop to the hospital.

Thanks to my phone, I arrived on time and did not need to ask many people for help. I felt happy and relaxed. Technology was very useful for me that day. It saved me time and stopped me from feeling lost.
